column1: # Signed i64 div/mod edge corpus — ONE source of truth for three tiers.
# enforced-by: RI-D1-PROFILE
# Consumers, all reading THIS file rather than a copy of it:
#   examples/mindc_mind/ri_d1_frozen_profile_gate.py   -> frozen-profile NATIVE ELF
#   tests/signed_div_mod_cross_backend_parity_run.rs   -> MLIR backend executable
#   src/eval/mod.rs / src/eval/ir_interp.rs unit tests -> the two INTERPRETER tiers
#     (same operand values, asserted on `apply_int_op` / `eval_ir` directly)
# "native == MLIR" is worth nothing if it is two lists that merely look alike and
# drift apart in one commit. A shared corpus makes the agreement structural: a
# fixture can only be edited for every tier at once, and a tier that stops reading
# this file stops being covered in a way `git diff` shows.
# The operand values are the ones the native emitter is pinned against in
# div_shift_cmp_edge_smoke.py (`nb_div_guarded`), extended with the two INT_MIN
# cases. The contract they encode, identical on every tier:
#   * truncation toward zero; remainder takes the sign of the DIVIDEND
#   * x / 0 == 0 and x % 0 == 0 — guarded, never a #DE / SIGFPE trap
#   * i64::MIN / -1 == i64::MIN and i64::MIN % -1 == 0 — the defined
#     two's-complement wrap (both backends substitute divisor 1)
# Every expected value is in 0..255, because the oracle is the process exit code
# (`fn main() -> i64` -> exit(rax), of which Linux keeps the low byte). A signal
# death reports a NEGATIVE returncode and is therefore always distinguishable
# from a legitimate answer — which is what makes "no trap" a testable claim.
# INT_MIN is built by negating INT_MAX and subtracting 1: `1 << 63` would be the
# obvious spelling but `Shl` is out of the frozen profile, and a most-negative
# literal has its own parse edge. The `==` comparison is what proves the VALUE,
# since an 8-bit exit code could not distinguish INT_MIN from 0.
# Columns (TAB-separated): name  expected_exit  kind  payload
#   kind=src   -> payload is the MIND source, on one line
#   kind=file  -> payload is a .mind filename in this directory
# Lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored by every reader.
div_basic
